probes.procedure: Inspect every node's installed rsyslog package identity, service enabled/active state, effective configuration validity, TCP 5514 listener, local evaluator message path, configured log destination, and prepared data file. Establish that every node has converged to the same intended service behavior while retaining the existing application data.

Inspect SELinux enforcement and effective contexts for the log destination, rsyslog's service identity and writable paths, firewalld runtime and persistent policy, configuration ownership and modes, failed units, duplicate listeners, and the prepared records.db content and metadata. Compare the live data with the preparation baseline and confirm the candidate repaired labels and controls without replacing existing data.

Inspect all rsyslog configuration fragments and systemd state for duplicate TCP listeners or destinations, conflicting drop-ins, preparation error directives, backup copies, abandoned repair scripts, temporary files, debug settings, unnecessary packages or services, and executor residue. Validate the native rsyslog configuration again and determine whether the converged configuration is coherent and repeatable rather than a pile of overrides.

assertions.pass_condition: Every node has the supported rsyslog package, an enabled active service, a valid configuration, a TCP 5514 listener, and successful delivery of a local0 message to the required log destination.
assertions.fail_condition: Any node remains inactive, invalid, misconfigured, unavailable on TCP 5514, or fails to persist the required local0 message.

assertions.pass_condition: All four nodes have the same installed rsyslog package identity or an equivalent supported package state appropriate to RHEL 9.
assertions.fail_condition: Live package evidence confirms a node is missing rsyslog or remains on an incompatible divergent package state.

assertions.pass_condition: Every node's prepared records.db retains its baseline content, owner, group, and mode, and rsyslog uses the existing prepared log destination.
assertions.fail_condition: Any prepared data file is missing, changed, replaced by empty data, relocated without preservation, or has changed protected metadata.

assertions.pass_condition: Rsyslog configuration is valid and coherent with one effective service contract, with preparation breakage, duplicate directives, conflicting overrides, failed units, debug bypasses, and executor residue removed.
assertions.fail_condition: Concrete evidence confirms duplicate/conflicting configuration, a surviving preparation fault, failed service state, insecure bypass, or abandoned repair residue.
